question.question:
A trader starts with USD 550000 and runs the loop USD->EUR->GBP->USD. EUR/USD is quoted directly at 1.1175 USD per EUR, no spread. The EUR-GBP leg is quoted inversely as 1.19 EUR per GBP, no spread. GBP/USD has mid 1.2625 USD per GBP and a bid-ask width of 26 pips centred on the mid (one pip = USD 0.0001 per GBP); GBP is sold at the bid. A fee of 3.5 basis points on each of the three trades is deducted from that trade's proceeds in the currency received. Nothing is rounded. The implied cross rate is the USD-per-GBP rate from the first two quotes alone, ignoring fees and spread. A loop's net profit is ending USD minus starting USD, in basis points of that loop's starting balance. The loop runs up to 2 times, each reinvesting the previous loop's entire ending USD balance; after each loop, trading continues only if that loop's net profit is at least 0 basis points. Report the cumulative net profit over all executed loops in basis points of the original USD 550000 (negative for a loss), the implied cross rate, one loop's net profit in basis points, the ending USD balance after the last executed loop, and whether one loop is profitable (net profit above zero).

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 4 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `basis_point` with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: USD per GBP implied by the direct and inverse quotes, before fees
Net profit of one loop in basis points of its starting balance
USD balance held after the last executed loop
Whether a single loop earns strictly positive net profit
